solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Opening lines in court

parts.note: an opening is a chance or opportunity
RY, short for railway, is the usual crossword abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: A barrister's first remarks delivered in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancery Division is a branch of the English High Court, so the word names a court.

clue.text: Persuasive businessman

parts.note: CO, company, is a business
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A businessman who is good at talking people round.
explanation.definitionFit: A forceful, convincing argument is one that persuades, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Arab accepts all the main headings in reply

indicators.note: the outer word takes in the compass letters

parts.note: Ar is the abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
the four cardinal compass points, N, S, W and E

explanation.surface: An Arab taking in every main heading of a document when responding.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply and a response are synonyms for something said back.

clue.text: Pack instrument for trickster

parts.note: a pack is a deck of cards
the harp is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A tool for packing things, offered to a con man.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat who wins at cards by sleight of hand is a kind of trickster.

clue.text: Film burglary by leader of gang raising the bar

parts.note: to film something is to record it
a break-in is a burglary

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Filming a burglary carried out by a gang boss lifting an iron bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting a new best mark is figuratively lifting the standard higher, as a high-jump bar is raised.

clue.text: A team's more popular numbers

parts.note: a team is a side, and with the apostrophe-s that gives side's

explanation.surface: A sports club's best-loved songs, as if fans sang them.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid enumerates this as (6), but it is the hyphenated A-SIDES; the apostrophe in 'team's' is ignored for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: On a vinyl single the A-side carried the track expected to be the hit, the flip side the lesser song.

clue.text: Forecaster is over beside lake

indicators.note: the little word is turned over, upside down in a down entry

parts.note: by means next to

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster's report finished, by a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world, one who foretold the future.

clue.text: Transfer county charge

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
a charge is a load, as in loading a gun

explanation.surface: A county council's fee for moving something.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying a file from a server to one's own computer is a transfer of data.

clue.text: Got down old Scandi books by new editor

indicators.note: the same word is made to do double duty, written upwards in a down entry

parts.note: the Eddas are medieval Icelandic collections of Norse myth and poetry

explanation.surface: Someone depressed by ancient Norse sagas next to a fresh editor.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has no reversal indicator of its own: 'down' is both part of the definition and, at a stretch, the signal to turn EDDAS round, a flaw the blog also notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To get someone down is to make them unhappy, the past tense matching the clue.

clue.text: Stop fighting, polish up still, hiding where the drink goes

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: to polish is to rub

indicators.note: the adverb conceals the drink phrase within it

parts.note: yet means still
down the hatch is a toast as one drinks, so the drink goes down the hatch

explanation.surface: Instructions to quit brawling, clean the distillery's still and hide the booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like distilling apparatus but is the adverb YET.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from a Native American custom of burying weapons to make peace, so it means end a quarrel.

clue.text: Stomach's wind spasm overcomes resistance

parts.note: wind in the body is gas

indicators.note: to overcome is pictured as going over and around, so the spasm word wraps the resistance letter

parts.note: a tic is a twitching spasm
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Abdominal wind and a cramp that defeat one's endurance.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the belly, as in a gastric ulcer, matching the possessive form of the clue word.

clue.text: Like a new fiddle that's free?

definitions.meaning: a brand-new violin has never had a bow drawn across it
unconquered, never having submitted to anyone

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what a violin fresh from the maker has in common with liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a definition by example, signalled by the question mark: the fiddle is not yet played with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone never forced to bend the head in submission remains free in spirit, undefeated and unsubdued.

clue.text: Wants current reversed between poles

indicators.note: the reversed river sits between the two pole letters

parts.note: north and south poles, N and S

indicators.note: the river name is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river, and a river is a current of water

explanation.surface: A desire for electricity flowing the wrong way across a battery's terminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks electrical, but it is a river; 'reversed' turns it round and 'between' sets it inside the two pole letters.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs both mean requires or lacks something, a synonym in the third person singular.

clue.text: Two blokes reportedly wasted cast

parts.note: two men's names, Roy and Al

indicators.note: says the next word is as it is heard spoken, not as it is written

parts.note: to have wasted money is to have blown it, past tense blew

explanation.surface: A pair of men drunk out of their minds, or thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns BLEW into the colour BLUE. 'cast' is a noun, a tinge of colour, not the verb throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast is a shade or tinge of colour, and this deep rich hue is one such shade.

clue.text: Deborah and Tracy misused source of energy

indicators.note: the letters of the two names are used in a wrong order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Two women, Deborah and Tracy, being badly treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugars and starches are the body's main fuel, so this food group is a supply of energy.

clue.text: Spent days downing cola for wind problem

indicators.note: the shuffled word drinks down, so swallows, the cola brand
used up or exhausted, so the letters of days fall apart and re-form

parts.note: Pepsi is a brand of cola

explanation.surface: Someone who has spent days drinking cola and is now bloated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent' scrambles the days word to DYSA, and 'downing' has it swallow the cola brand after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion often brings belching and flatulence, so it is a problem involving wind.

clue.text: Two idiots batting hit man

indicators.note: says the fool word appears twice

parts.note: an ass is an idiot
a cricketer who is batting is in

explanation.surface: A pair of fools at the crease, one of whom strikes a man.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract killer, hired to murder, is a professional killer of targets.

clue.text: Rent reduction causing little sign of emotion

parts.note: a rent is a rip or tear in cloth
a drop is a reduction, as in a price drop

explanation.surface: A cut in rent that makes a tenant weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is a rip.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop shed from the eye is a small outward show of feeling.

clue.text: Pricey French article to engrave for obstacle race

parts.note: a steep price is a high one
le is French for the
to chase metal is to engrave or emboss it

explanation.surface: An expensive French item being engraved as a prize for a race over hurdles.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or running race over fences, ditches and water jumps is run around a course of obstacles.

clue.text: Writer's regrettably given up Italian food

indicators.note: in a down entry the letters are presented upwards, reversed

parts.note: the writer's means I am, I'm, from the setter's point of view
alas expresses regret

explanation.surface: A writer sadly having to give up Italian cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: This spiced cured sausage is a classic product of Italian cookery.

clue.text: Plant needs IT installed for speed

indicators.note: the plant, with the two letters put in, would stand for the speed word, so they come out of it

parts.note: celerity is a literary word for swiftness

explanation.surface: A factory that needs computer systems installed to work faster.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: CELERY with IT put in gives CELERITY, speed. 'Plant' looks like a factory and 'IT' like computing.
explanation.definitionFit: The crunchy green stalked vegetable grows as a garden plant.

clue.text: Sudden low pressure stopping top-class missile

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI with the figure one read as letter I

indicators.note: the pressure letter plugs, or stops, a gap in the missile word

parts.note: a rocket is a missile
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A weather report: a sudden low-pressure zone halting an elite missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sudden low pressure' reads as one weather phrase, but 'pressure' belongs to the wordplay; 'stopping' puts P inside ROCKET after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch of thin or downdraughting air makes an aircraft drop abruptly, a sudden low point in flight.

clue.text: One gets this often by eating something enticing initially

definitions.text: One gets this often by eating something enticing initially

indicators.note: the opening letters of the five preceding words are taken

explanation.surface: A warning that tempting snacks make a person fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitually overeating tempting food can leave a person grossly overweight.

clue.text: Bypass English Channel on return trip

indicators.note: the letters travel back the way they came, read from the end

parts.note: Dave is a UK television channel

explanation.surface: Skipping England and the Channel while coming home from a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: DAVE is a British TV channel; 'English Channel' looks like the sea strait. 'on return trip' reverses EDAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass a problem is to dodge or avoid it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Theatre worker and caviar supplier short of time

indicators.note: lacking, so the time letter is removed from the fish

parts.note: caviar is the roe of the sturgeon fish

explanation.surface: A stagehand who also sells caviar but is always running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' is the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Operations take place in an operating theatre, so a doctor who operates works there.

clue.text: Head office put on The Prisoner for money

parts.note: to put on a play is to stage it

explanation.surface: Head office mounting a production of The Prisoner, the 1960s TV series, for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive held until a ransom is paid is a prisoner kept for money.

clue.text: Record husband visiting latest relative

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the record and husband letters enter the latest word

parts.note: the latest thing is the new one
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A recording of a husband dropping in on his newest relation.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's son is a family relation.

clue.text: Member of CID's in nick with Yankee regularly

indicators.note: the detective goes inside the theft word

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal
a DI, detective inspector, is a member of the CID, Britain's plain-clothes detective branch; 's stands for is
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A detective sitting in a police station alongside an American, on a routine basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' looks like a police station (British slang) but is the verb steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at a steady, even rate is doing it in a regular way, an adverb synonym.
